title: I have made a database investigation game set on Titan inspired from Lost Wiki Kozlovka
author: miculpionier
selftext:
I have made a game about chemosynthetic life being discovered on Titan at a base maintained by only a single supervisor and robots and being hacked for the purpose of extracting hydrogen produced by those lifeforms, hydrogen that is labeled as green but is actually gray, without any consideration for their livelihoods.

I have inspired myself from RADIOSOL, Lost Wiki Kozlovka, Molleindustria and my obsession with prefabricated, modernist buildings that I see every day. I have also inspired myself from the really bad, earlier stances of people like Sam Altman on the future of AI, that AI will always be beneficial to humanity when it's often not the case. It also inspired by cases where market interest conflicts with public interest, and besides that I cannot say more here to not provoke discontent, more is in the game and concept files.

The nature of chemosynthesis on worlds like Titan is disputed, but here I wondered what if chemosynthetic alien life was discovered just like the Earth has deep biosphere.

I decided the concept and art direction while Claude Opus 5.5 implemented most of the code and drawn the SVGs and JS-based assets. Codex and other smaller models helped when I reached usage limits.

The latest version of the game is here: [https://miculpionier.ro/projects/selk-terminal](https://miculpionier.ro/projects/selk-terminal/)  
The source code is here: [https://gitlab.com/window-ops-web/selk-terminal](https://gitlab.com/window-ops-web/selk-terminal)  
You can also try the game in itch: [https://vb2020.itch.io/selk](https://vb2020.itch.io/selk)

Note: The mast in the trailer does not match the mast in the game because the mast in the game is an older SVG-based asset designed in earlier stages of development while the mast in the trailer is a newer, JS-based asset designed specifically for cool effects like inclination and shaking with a rigid body. Porting the trailer asset into the game would be a lot of work on top of other more important priorities in the development of this game or my life. I sometimes sat for eight hours straight into the night to resolve bugs, introduce new features and other stuff that has nothing to do with the core logic, but only so as to not get hate.

This is a real recording of how I complete the first report of the game, I don't spoil everything so as to calm spirits, this is a database investigation after all:

https://reddit.com/link/1wz9tp7/video/je85nu4w0wth1/player
